newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila interbank rate softens in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila interbank rate softens in liquid market.

text.p: * Done rate hits a high of 13.59375 pct
The Philippine interbank call loan rate slid to 12.59375 percent on Thursday from the previous 12.78125 percent on improved liquidity, dealers said.
"The heavy intervention of the Central Bank in the foreign exchange market in the past two days has finally stabilised the local currency," said one trader.
The Central Bank kept its overnight borrowing rate at 12.5 percent and its lending rate at 14.5 percent after it stemmed speculation on the peso following the steep drop in treasury bill notes.
The bank had increased its overnight rates on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Done rates in the interbank market hit a high of 13.59375 percent and a low of 12.53125 percent.
Some 13.977 billion pesos changed hands among 23 lenders and 24 borrowers.
Secondary trading of government securities was slow with the three-month bills pegged at 11.65 percent, six-month bills at 11.975 percent, and one-year bills at 12.6 percent.
Traders said they expected the Central Bank to drop its overnight rates in the next few days with the fall of the August inflation rate and as the foreign exchange market continue to stabilise.
